Interface Element

All Known Implementing Classes:
BarChartElement, CalendarElement, CanvasElement, ChartElement, Column, ColumnsElement, Component, ContainerElement, DialogElement, DockElement, DualSparklineElement, ErrorPlaceholder, FlowElement, FormElement, FormFieldElement, GaugeElement, GenericWidgetElement, GridElement, InlineScopeElement, LazyElement, LineGaugeElement, ListElement, MarkdownElement, MarkupTextAreaElement, MarkupTextElement, Panel, RichTextAreaElement, RichTextElement, Row, ScrollableElement, ScrollbarElement, Spacer, SparklineElement, SpinnerElement, StackElement, StyledElement, TableElement, TabsElement, TextAreaElement, TextElement, TextInputElement, TreeElement, WaveTextElement
public interface Element
Base interface for all DSL elements. Elements represent UI components that can be rendered to a frame.

Elements can handle events by implementing event handler methods or by registering handler lambdas. Events propagate through the element tree and can be consumed to stop propagation.

    • render

      void render(Frame frame, Rect area, RenderContext context)
      Renders this element to the given frame within the specified area.
      Parameters:
      frame - the frame to render to
      area - the area to render within
      context - the render context providing focus and state information

    • constraint

      default Constraint constraint()
      Returns the layout constraint for this element, if any. Used by container elements to determine sizing.
      Returns:
      the constraint, or null if the element should use default sizing

    • preferredSize

      Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
